mission: Mine every rights-cleared, Linux-available per-frame artifact in the repo for natural occurrences of six multi-paddle hazard scenarios (foreign paddle near target, crossing paddles, partner/opponent paddle in frame, idle target wrist with moving nearby paddle, two paddles inside torso-normalized reach, occlusion-induced identity swaps); emit a Tier-C candidate list, reviewable frame packs, and a frozen annotation queue + label schema for future human review. Nothing is called Gold.
method: Deterministic geometric miner (tools/mining/wave_g_g03_multi_paddle_miner.py) over three committed signal sources: (1) machine paddle-detector boxes in datasets/paddle-bench/ownership-review/queue.json (score >= 0.30); (2) Wave-C ownership paddle points (target + other) in bundles/*/annotation/devin-visual-v2-waveC-ownership.json, used only as seed coordinates; (3) Apple-Vision pose tracks in datasets/paddle-bench/runs-wave-a/*/people.json for torso-normalized reach (2.2x shoulder-hip length), wrist velocity, and pose-bbox-overlap identity-swap risk. Candidates deduplicated per (scenario, case, 150 ms). Crops extracted with ffmpeg only where a committed clip.mp4 exists (afn-sasebo-rally1, wm-volley-02); all other frame-pack entries carry timestamps/coordinates only because source videos are gitignored on Linux. All inputs SHA-256 fingerprinted in candidates.json meta.provenance.

datasetScope.grouping: All mined material is pinned dev (datasets/corpus/splits.json); recordings are DVIDS/AFN PD-USGov and licensed wm-tournament footage per datasets/corpus/sources.json.

holdoutStatement: wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were excluded by case ID before any of their records entered mining state: their queue.json frames, bundle annotations, and clip.mp4 were never inspected, counted, cropped, or emitted. The miner hard-fails if a held-out ID appears in its output; outputs were additionally grepped clean.
findings: Multi-paddle co-presence is pervasive in the dev pool: 54 partner/opponent-in-frame candidates across 8 of 10 minable cases, so ownership disambiguation is not an edge case.
34 candidates put two paddle observations inside one torso-normalized reach disc (6 cases) - the exact geometry where the tracker's S3/S4 ownership failures were previously observed.

28 occlusion/identity-swap risk frames were found from pose-bbox overlap (with confidence-dip flags) plus overlapping detector boxes; these are the natural candidates for the flip-truncation failure family proven by workstream B.

crossing_paddles produced 0 candidates from 23 consecutive labeled intervals: at the ~250 ms ownership-label sampling rate, labeled-point segment intersection is too coarse to catch crossings. SCIENTIFIC_NEGATIVE for this detection route; dense paddle tracks (Mac-only) or denser labels are needed.
idle_wrist_moving_nearby_paddle found exactly 1 candidate (wavea-944403-dink, ~22464 ms) - the sparse label sampling limits recall here too; the detector logic is in place for dense tracks.
Source videos and canonical run dirs are gitignored on Linux, so crops exist only for the 2 cases with committed clip.mp4; all other frame packs are timestamp/coordinate packs by necessity.
tierStatement: Every candidate and queue entry is machine-proposed Tier-C. Human ownership labels were consumed only as seed coordinates; scenario assignments are miner proposals. Nothing here is Gold; the frozen queue exists precisely so a future human pass can produce Gold.

gates.note: No production TypeScript/Swift code was modified; changes are a Python mining tool plus dataset artifacts.

verdictRationale: Mining succeeded with real counts for 4 of 6 scenarios (129 Tier-C candidates, frozen queue + schema delivered), but crossing_paddles is a measured 0 (label sampling too coarse - honest negative, not absence of the phenomenon) and idle-wrist recall is limited to 1 by the same sparsity. Dense per-frame paddle tracks (Mac-only extraction) are required to mine those two scenarios properly, so this is YELLOW rather than PROVISIONAL_GREEN.
